newsitem.title: USA: Armey still hopes for budget deal with White House.
newsitem.headline: Armey still hopes for budget deal with White House.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey said Tuesday he had not given up hope of a budget deal with the White House and expected a budget resolution on the House floor in early May.

Armey said any budget package had to include a healthy tax cut, calling for a 50 percent cut in capital gains taxes along with a mechanism to account for inflation, reduction or elimination of estate taxes and a $500 tax credit for children. "I'm certainly not ready to quit on the (budget) talks," Amrey said. He told reporters he had an "encouraging" talk with White House chief of staff Erskine Bowles last week.
Armey said that going beyond those options would depend on tax committees finding some offsetting savings. He said the cost of the tax cuts would depend on precisely how they were structured.
"From my discussions with the chief of staff last week I am encouraged to belive we can get to a satisfactory number on taxes between us," Armey said.
Armey said he did not see any reluctance on the part of Bowles for a sizable tax cut, but did not specify a dollar amount that House Republicans wanted.
Senate Republicans have pushed for tax cuts totalling about $200 billion over five years, the White House wants roughly half that amount.
